- When sentiment is high (≥0.8), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reverting trend.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after price peaks.
- Forecast mean reverts too slowly; apply a 3–5 day smoothing filter to reduce overshoot.
- In early horizon (first 5–7 days), model underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.5% buffer for downside risk.
- When sentiment + price history shows strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture continuation; add 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is rising and price is trending up, model tends to peak too early; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days.
